# Psalm 106 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Hallelujah! Give thanks to the LORD because he is good — his faithful love lasts forever!

**2** Who could ever fully describe the LORD's mighty acts? Who could proclaim all his praise?

**3** How happy are those who act justly and do what is right at all times!

**4** Remember me, LORD, when you bless your people! Come to my rescue when you save them!

**5** Let me share in the prosperity of your chosen people, celebrate with your nation, and join your people in praising you.

**6** We have sinned, just like our ancestors. We have done wrong. We have acted wickedly.

**7** When our ancestors were in Egypt, they didn't appreciate your miracles. They forgot how often you showed them love. They rebelled right there at the Red Sea.

**8** But he saved them anyway — to defend the honor of his name and demonstrate his power.

**9** He commanded the Red Sea and it dried up. He walked them through the deep ocean floor as easily as through a desert.

**10** He rescued them from the enemy and freed them from their oppressors.

**11** The water rushed back and covered their enemies — not a single one survived.

**12** Then his people believed his promises and sang his praises.

**13** But they quickly forgot everything he did. They didn't wait for his guidance.

**14** They gave in to intense cravings in the wilderness and tested God in the wasteland.

**15** He gave them what they demanded — but sent a plague along with it.

**16** In the camp, they became jealous of Moses and of Aaron, the LORD's holy priest.

**17** The ground split open and swallowed Dathan; it buried Abiram's whole group.

**18** Fire blazed among their followers; flames consumed the wicked.

**19** At Mount Horeb they built a calf and worshiped a statue made of metal.

**20** They traded the glorious God for a statue of a bull that eats grass!

**21** They forgot the God who saved them — the one who had done such great things in Egypt,

**22** miracles in the land of Ham, terrifying acts at the Red Sea.

**23** So God said he would destroy them — but Moses, his chosen servant, stepped into the gap and talked God out of destroying them.

**24** Then they rejected the beautiful promised land; they didn't trust God's word.

**25** They complained inside their tents and refused to listen to the LORD.

**26** So he raised his hand and swore that he would let them die in the desert,

**27** and would scatter their descendants among the nations, spread across foreign lands.

**28** Then they joined the worship of Baal at Peor and ate food sacrificed to lifeless gods.

**29** They provoked the LORD with their behavior, and a plague swept through the camp.

**30** But Phinehas stood up and took action, and the plague stopped.

**31** This was credited to him as a righteous act — remembered forever, generation after generation.

**32** They also made God angry at the waters of Meribah, and Moses suffered because of them.

**33** They pushed him so hard that he spoke without thinking.

**34** They didn't destroy the nations as the LORD had commanded.

**35** Instead they mixed in with those peoples and adopted their practices.

**36** They worshiped their idols, and those idols became a death trap.

**37** They sacrificed their own sons and daughters to demons!

**38** They spilled innocent blood — the blood of their own children — sacrificed to Canaan's idols. And the land was poisoned with blood.

**39** They made themselves filthy by what they did — they were completely unfaithful.

**40** The LORD's anger burned against his people; he was disgusted with his own people.

**41** He handed them over to the nations, and their enemies ruled over them.

**42** Their enemies crushed them and kept them under their thumb.

**43** Time after time he rescued them, but they kept rebelling and sinking deeper into sin.

**44** Even so, he paid attention to their suffering when he heard them crying out.

**45** He remembered his covenant for their sake and softened because of his enormous faithful love.

**46** He made their captors treat them with mercy.

**47** Save us, LORD our God! Bring us back from among the nations so we can thank your holy name and celebrate your praises!

**48** Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting! Let everyone say 'Amen!' Hallelujah!

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **106:6-7**: The psalm begins with confession: 'We have sinned, just like our ancestors.' This isn't finger-pointing at the past — it's owning the same pattern in the present.

- **106:43-45**: 'Time after time he rescued them, but they kept rebelling.' And yet — 'He remembered his covenant.' That's the whole Bible in two sentences: human unfaithfulness met by divine faithfulness.

— PNEUMA
